bullets.text: Rebar +INR1,650/t w-w to INR62,100/t while HRC holds flat at INR63,800/t, narrowing the flat-long spread to ~INR1,700/t.
bullets.source: Nomura — India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 25 Sep 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura says India steel prices stay firm, led by a renewed rebar uptrend that has narrowed the flat-long spread after months of long-product weakness since 1QFY27, with HRC near four-year highs.
points: INR63,800/t HRC, flat w-w, near 4-yr high

bullets.text: Imported coking coal fell $6/t w-w to $276/t, still above Aug-26's $232/t average; India HRC spot margin ~INR37,540/t.
bullets.source: Nomura — India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 25 Sep 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura notes imported coking coal eased w-w but remains well above August levels after supply disruptions, geopolitics and a fatal Chinese mine accident drove a spike; India's HRC margin sits just under the 2QFY27F average.

bullets.text: Kotak: cement sector market cap +31% (~Rs1.6tn) over five years, all of it from UltraTech — the bull narratives created no wealth.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] Strategy: The curious case of the Indian cement sector

detail.summary: Kotak's strategy note argues five years of bull narratives (GST-cut price stickiness, Adani-led consolidation, limestone scarcity, branding, green fuel savings) produced almost no wealth creation, since the entire market-cap gain came from one stock.

bullets.text: Kotak says Street 2HFY27 numbers assume price hikes and softer costs it does not see; expects no positive earnings surprises.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] Strategy: The curious case of the Indian cement sector

detail.summary: Kotak expects depressed near-term profitability from high input costs, arguing Street numbers bake in 2HFY27 price hikes and/or lower costs its own estimates do not support.
points: 2HFY27 Street assumes hikes and cost relief
No supply-demand improvement for next few years

bullets.text: NMDC raised lump prices INR150/t to INR5,400/t effective Sep-26; fines held flat at INR4,500/t.
bullets.source: Nomura — India steel - Steel weekly trends (week ended 25 Sep 2026)

detail.summary: Nomura flags NMDC's domestic ore hike against a stable seaborne backdrop, with 62% Fe CFR China ore sitting near its CY26 low.
points: Near CY26 YTD low for seaborne ore

bullets.text: Kotak expects Infosys to cut FY27 guide to 1.5-2.5% (from 1.5-3%) and HCLT to raise to 3-4%; Wipro guided -2% to 0%.

detail.summary: Kotak's 2QFY27 preview argues demand is flat versus the June quarter, AI deflation (~7% gross, 3.5% net) is becoming visible in operating metrics even as rupee depreciation props up margins, and mid-tiers (PSYS, Coforge, MPHL) outgrow large caps this quarter.

bullets.text: Mphasis reiterated ~3% CC QoQ for 2Q (highest in 3 years) and its 14.75-15.75% FY27 EBIT margin guide at JPM's IR meeting.
bullets.source: JPM — Mphasis: Demand stable and guidance intact

detail.summary: JPM hosted Mphasis' IR head: demand unchanged given low exposure to tariff-hit verticals, TCV conversion on track, and margins recover from 2Q as utilization improves after contract-buyout costs. JPM stays Overweight, PT Rs2,650.
points: FY27 growth: high-single to low-double digits

bullets.text: Hexaware kept CY26 growth guide at 6-7%, needing 2.7% CQGR in 3Q-4Q for the midpoint; JPM stays Neutral.
bullets.source: JPM — Hexaware: CY26 revenue guidance maintained, optimistic on CY27

detail.summary: Hexaware told JPM it won most vendor-consolidation reviews across 13 of its top 20 clients, but that cost growth as clients held back spend elsewhere; AI deflation ~2%/yr now, seen at 20-25% cumulative over four years.
points: 6-7% CY26 guide, lower end more likely
Won consolidation at 13 of top 20 clients

bullets.text: Nifty rebalance at Tue 29 Sep close: BSE ~$617mn passive buying, VAML $144mn; Wipro -$151mn, IH -$129mn.
bullets.source: Kotak — [Kotak] Nifty Indices Changes (Close of Tuesday, 29th September)

detail.summary: The note recaps the Nifty50/Next50/Bank Nifty/CPSE reconstitution effective Tuesday's close with estimated passive flows per name, flagging which stocks face flows worth several multiples of ADV.

bullets.text: UBS India-CEI +0.7% m/m in August (July +0.4%); a $100/bbl Brent case cuts FY27 GDP ~20bp and lifts CPI to 5.5%.
bullets.source: UBS — UBS India: what's trending in India's macro

detail.summary: UBS argues resilient domestic activity should buffer India against external headwinds, but spells out a downside: if Brent averages $100/bbl through FY27, growth slows, inflation runs hotter, the current account widens and the RBI turns more hawkish.
points: RBI seen 50bp cumulative hikes from October

bullets.text: BofA Flow Show keeps long equities/short duration; favours commodities and EM over cyclicals after a two-month Xi-Trump truce to 10 Jan.
bullets.source: BofA — BofA ASIA Daily: XI-TRUMP Truce | APAC Strategy | FLOW SHOW (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: BofA reads the Xi-Trump summit as diplomacy over substance — a truce extension to Jan 10 with rare-earth friction unresolved — and keeps clients biased toward commodities and EM over cyclicals given how far US nominal GDP has outrun long bonds.
points: US nominal GDP +63% over six years

bullets.text: BofA Vahan: Sep retail 2W +29% YoY (EV 11%), MHCV +36%, LCV +21%; tractors -1%; picks AL, TMCV, Hyundai, Bajaj Auto.
bullets.source: BofA — Autos - India: Channel checks & Vahan tracker: who's winning; who's losing?

detail.summary: BofA reads September's strong 2W/PV/CV retail as base- and GST-driven rather than fresh acceleration — tractors already softening and growth should moderate into festive on tougher comps; margin pressure and EPS cuts not fully behind.
points: Picks: AL, TMCV, Hyundai, Bajaj Auto

bullets.text: Elara: unregistered low-speed e-2W hit 1.8mn units in FY26 (56% of e2W), understating 2W growth and threatening Hero's entry franchise.
bullets.source: Elara — Automobiles - Reshaping of entry level 2W mobility - Sector Update

detail.summary: Elara argues reported 2W and EV-penetration data understate the market: including unregistered low-speed e-2W, FY26 volume is ~24.0mn (+15.1%) vs reported 22.1mn (+10.2%). The unbranded segment substitutes for economy motorcycles, reframing Hero's entry weakness as structural.

ai_semis.text: Anthropic reportedly in talks to lease up to 1GW of compute ($40bn+ implied) and signed a 7-year $11.6bn CPU deal with Akamai.
TSMC reportedly plans five new advanced-packaging fabs as AI demand surges.
GS sees hyperscaler AI capex at $1.2tn in 2027 and $1.4tn in 2028, needing ~$300bn annual AI revenue to break even.
ai_semis.source: GS — [GS Daily] Trump-Xi First Read ... US Strategy on AI Capex
